newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA OIL BASKET DROPS 10 CENTS IN WEEK.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA OIL BASKET DROPS 10 CENTS IN WEEK.

text.p: Venezuela's basket of crude oil and refined products shed ten cents over the week to close Friday at $16.10 per barrel, the Energy and Mines Ministry said in a statement.

Traders in the price-setting futures markets of New York and London attributed the fall to Iraq's imminent resumption of oil exports after a two-month interruption in its UN-sponsored export programme.
The average basket price for August so far was $16.43 per barrel, against a $15.80 average for July and $15.30 in June.
The basket fell steadily in the first half of the year after hitting a multi-year high of $21.55 per barrel in December 1996.
The basket closed that year with one of the highest average prices for several years at $18.39 per barrel, against $14.84 for 1995.
In 1997 so far, the basket average was $16.59 per barrel, the Ministry said, one cent below last week's figure and well above the government's budgeted average of $14.40.
For 1998, the government budgeted for an average price of $15.50 per barrel.
